ai.title: Disable middleware for websocket init action
ai.summary: Removed `protec.run` wrapper from `subscribeToAction('init', ...)` in `backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts`. The `onInit` handler now executes without authentication middleware. This change prevents middleware interference during the initial websocket handshake.

eli5.text: When you connect to the assistant over a live websocket session, the first handshake message now skips the login/security check that earlier forced every message through authentication. That only affects the very first message in a session; everything after the connection is established still goes through the normal verification. The change landed in the backend on 2024-10-05 and is live today, so sessions now start up faster but are not less secure once running.

ai.title: Init action now fingerprint-protected
ai.summary: WebSocket middleware inserts missing fingerprints via onConflictDoNothing before quota checks. Init action now runs through protec.run, enforcing fingerprint validation. New error action type added to SERVER_ACTION_SCHEMA to relay middleware halts to clients. Covers backend/src/websockets/middleware.ts, backend/src/websockets/websocket-action.ts, common/src/actions.ts.

eli5.text: Starting now, the connection check that begins your session now requires a valid device fingerprint, so freshly started sessions are screened the same way as regular actions. If that check fails, your client receives a short error message instead of silently being dropped. The error message type and relay path were also added so these halts can reach you.

ai.title: Increase stream buffer size in process-stream.ts
ai.summary: Bumped `bufferSize` constant from 50 to 150 in `backend/src/process-stream.ts`. This change expands the internal string accumulation limit for stream processing, likely to accommodate larger chunks or reduce frequent flushing. Affects tag processing and attribute parsing within the backend stream handler.

eli5.text: The assistant's text-reading system now temporarily holds more content before processing it, increasing from 50 to 150 pieces at a time. This mainly affects how the backend handles streaming data, making the processing smoother for larger chunks of information. You wouldn't directly notice this change, but it helps the system handle incoming data more efficiently behind the scenes. This is an internal adjustment that's already live today.

ai.title: URL scraping moves from client to CLI
ai.summary: URL scraping logic relocated from `npm-app/src/client.ts` to `npm-app/src/cli.ts`. Previously, `Client` mutated the last user message with scraped content before sending. Now, `CLI` parses URLs from `userInput` and prepends scraped blocks to the message content before storage. This ensures scraping occurs on raw user input rather than potentially edited or stored message states.

eli5.text: When you paste a link into a chat, the assistant will now fetch and include the page content immediately, based solely on what you type, before that message gets stored or edited. This moves web-link fetching from the background message-handling layer into the chat-entry point, so scraped text is attached to your original input rather than a later-edited version of your message. It is live today for anyone using the command-line interface to chat.

ai.title: Add optional initial prompt arg to manicode CLI
ai.summary: Manicode CLI now accepts a second argument, `[initial-prompt]`, which is immediately processed as the first user input upon startup. `printInitialPrompt` in `npm-app/src/cli.ts` writes the provided string to stdout and triggers `handleUserInput`, bypassing the interactive prompt wait. The entry logic in `npm-app/src/index.ts` parses `process.argv.slice(3)` and updates the help text to reflect the new optional parameter.

eli5.text: You can now start the coding assistant with a pre-typed message by adding words after the project folder when you launch it, so it jumps straight into working on that instruction without making you type it yourself. The assistant reads that extra text, prints it on the screen as if you had entered it, and immediately begins handling it like any other question you'd ask. This is a small convenience that only affects the program's command-line startup behavior; it does not change how the assistant works once you're already using it.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.81
ai.summary: Version in npm-app/package.json bumped from 1.0.80 to 1.0.81. Internal release update.

eli5.text: If you open the app today, the assistant can start a conversation using a prompt you provide right when it launches, so you can hand it a task and start working immediately instead of typing your first message. Behind the scenes, the app also builds a protective marker during startup checks, and large batches of data now flow through with a bigger capacity, which reduces stalls during heavy work. These changes are part of the October 5, 2024 release, so they are live now if you are on the latest version.
